profile.summary: Graph_RG is a protein-ligand binding affinity predictor that does not need a docked pose or a complex structure. It was the author's entry in the small molecule affinity prediction category of CASP16, the 2024 community prediction experiment. Because it does not search over conformations, the author reports it as fast enough for very large virtual screens. The sources read name no code or weights and the paper is not open access, so what the model reads as input and how it is built are not described here.

summary_quotes.text: we present Graph_RG, our top-performing model in the CASP16 small molecule track's protein-ligand affinity prediction category
Graph_RG is noncomplex dependent, hence exhibits exceptional computational efficiency

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The sources that could be read do not describe the architecture. The abstract says only that the method is pose-free and not dependent on the protein-ligand complex, which is what the author credits for its speed, and that possible improvements include dataset optimisation, atomic vector representation and model architecture upgrades. The paper itself is not open access and no repository is named in the sources read, so the layers, the training objective and the input features are not established here. The record's own description calls it a two-stream graph transformer; no source read states that.

quotes.text: A Pose-Free Framework for Billion-Scale Virtual Screening
We further discuss the potential improvements for Graph_RG, including dataset optimization, atomic vector representation enhancements, and model architecture upgrades.

sections.title: What the author reports
sections.body: The abstract reports an N-weighted Kendall's Tau of 0.42 in the CASP16 affinity prediction category, with the second best submission at 0.36, and claims operation more than 100 000 times faster than methods that depend on a conformation search, which the author says enables screening at the billion to ten billion scale on standard servers. These are the author's own figures, taken from the abstract; the full text, the assessors' numbers and the evaluation set were not read.

quotes.text: achieving a N-weighted Kendall's Tau of 0.42-significantly outperforming other submissions (second-best: 0.36)
operating > 100 000× faster than conformation-search dependent prediction methods, thus enabling billion- to 10-billion-scale screening on standard servers

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: There is nothing to pin. No repository, no checkpoint and no version identifier for Graph_RG is named in the sources read. The abstract mentions derivative models and an interactive web platform to host them, described as a development the author points out rather than a resource that exists at a given address. A result produced with Graph_RG today cannot be reproduced from public artefacts, and the only fixed reference is the paper, Proteins volume 94, pages 286 to 294, first published 2025-06-20 and printed in the January 2026 issue.

notes: Kept as a page rather than a stub because Graph_RG has a paper of its own (Zhang, Proteins 94:286-294, doi 10.1002/prot.70010) even though nothing is released; everything on the page comes from that paper's abstract as served by Europe PMC. The record description calls Graph_RG a two-stream graph transformer and a structure-based model; the abstract supports neither, and says the method is pose-free and not complex dependent, so the description may need correcting. The record's existing source, the Wang and Cheng 2026 leakage-controlled benchmark, is bioRxiv only (pdf at https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.09.17.752433v1.full.pdf) and was not fetched in this pass. The Europe PMC record shows no PMC copy of the Graph_RG paper. If a reviewer has journal access, the full text would fill in architecture, inputs and training data, all marked unextracted here.
